1. Project Overview & Business Scenario

Business Context: A digital media organization seeks to automatically detect and flag misleading or fabricated news articles prior to publishing. With thousands of articles submitted daily, manual editorial verification is slow and resource-intensive. The objective is to build an intelligent NLP classification system that distinguishes genuine reporting from fabricated disinformation using writing patterns, textual tokens, and vocabulary structures.

1.1 Objectives Achieved

  • Raw Text Cleaning & Lemmatization: Converted unstructured raw text into normalized lemma tokens by stripping HTML, URLs, symbols, digits, and redundant stopwords.
  • Linguistic Feature Extraction: Combined headline semantics, body text, article length metrics, and uppercase capitalization ratios.
  • Feature Engineering: Transformed cleaned text into high-dimensional TF-IDF matrices (unigrams & bigrams, 8,000 features).
  • Model Benchmarking: Trained and tuned 4 industry-standard classifiers: Linear Support Vector (LinearSVC), Logistic Regression, Passive Aggressive Classifier, and Multinomial Naive Bayes.
  • Rigorous Evaluation: Evaluated using Precision, Recall, F1-Score, Confusion Matrices, and ROC-AUC curves.
  • Deployment: Packaged an interactive Gradio GUI for real-time news authenticity prediction with confidence percentages.

2. Dataset Exploration & Preprocessing

The model was trained on the benchmark Kaggle Fake News dataset comprising 6,335 articles with a balanced 50:50 class distribution (3,171 REAL and 3,164 FAKE news stories).

2.1 Text Preprocessing Pipeline

  1. Lowercasing: Uniformly converted all text characters to lowercase.
  2. Regular Expression Filtering: Removed hyperlinks (http/www), HTML markup, numbers, and special symbols.
  3. Stopword Removal: Stripped English stopwords (NLTK corpus) such as auxiliary verbs and common prepositions.
  4. WordNet Lemmatization: Reduced words to their base dictionary root forms (e.g., "claimed" → "claim").
Sample Transformation:
Raw: "BREAKING: NASA Rover Discovers Ancient Lake Bed on Mars at http://nasa.gov/rover!"
Cleaned Tokens: nasa rover discovers ancient lake bed mars

4. Model Training & Evaluation Metrics

The dataset was split into 80% Training (5,068 articles) and 20% Testing (1,267 articles) with stratification to preserve class balance. Text was transformed via TF-IDF vectorization with unigram and bigram n-grams (8,000 maximum features).

4.3 Misclassification & Error Analysis

  • False Positives (Real news predicted as Fake): Articles containing satire, quoted opinion pieces, or editorial columns occasionally share lexical patterns with sensationalist writing.
  • False Negatives (Fake news predicted as Real): Elaborate fake news articles that mimic formal AP/Reuters journalistic style with neutral wording are more challenging to differentiate purely on lexical unigrams, benefiting from n-gram bigram features.

5. Production Cloud Deployment & RAG Document Pipeline

Beyond local evaluation, the news classification system was containerized and deployed into production on Vercel Serverless Cloud. It features a custom White Theme Web Application with real-time inference and a dedicated Retrieval-Augmented (RAG) Document Pipeline for verifying multi-page PDF documents.

Live Production Web Deployment: https://fakenewsclassification.vercel.app
Features dual-mode real-time article verification, multi-page PDF document fact-checking, Explainable AI trigger keywords, and sub-15ms serverless inference.

5.2 RAG Document Ingestion & Claim-by-Claim Fact-Checking

The system integrates a Retrieval-Augmented Claim Verification Pipeline tailored for news editors and researchers:

  • Document Ingestion & Page Extraction: High-throughput text parsing across multi-page PDFs using pypdf.
  • Semantic Claim Chunking: The document is partitioned into coherent informational assertion blocks (20–50 words), filtering noise, headers, and boilerplate.
  • Factual Integrity Audit: Each claim is evaluated against the trained decision boundary, producing a granular per-page audit table with confidence metrics and influential trigger keywords.
  • Aggregated Authenticity Scoring: The system produces an overall document health percentage and risk classification (AUTHENTIC vs. SUSPICIOUS).

5.3 Local Gradio Interface (Offline Standalone)

In addition to the Vercel web deployment, a local GUI is provided via gradio_app.py on port 7860 for offline desktop environments.

6. Conclusion & Final Submission Deliverables

The project successfully meets all academic and industry requirements of Project Statement 15. The Linear Support Vector machine achieved state-of-the-art text classification performance with 93.69% accuracy, an F1-Score of 0.9367, and an ROC-AUC of 0.9833 on unseen holdout test articles.
